title: A gym still on its first owner login sees "by Owner (old owner key)" next to a reward it gave
what: When nobody is signed in by name (a gym that never moved to the staff sign-in), the server writes the person as "Owner (old owner key)". That text comes back to the admin app: the workout offer list prints "Extended free by 3 days (reward) · by Owner (old owner key)". The same words are saved as who accepted the terms, who changed the reminder switches and who downloaded the whole copy. A receipt changed straight in the database is saved as "Database (postgres)". "Old owner key" and "postgres" are our inside words; an owner does not know them.
expected: The owner sees a plain name such as "Owner" (or the gym owner name) wherever the server says who did something.
who: owners of gyms that never moved to staff sign-in
how_often: every reward, terms tick or download made from the first owner login
fix_line: Write a plain "Owner" instead of the inside words, and change the rows already saved

title: A test gym with the old name "ForgeAI Test Gym" and a sample shop is made on the live server
what: A database change file makes a gym called "ForgeAI Test Gym" with the code FORGE1 and fills its shop with sample products, and tops the stock back up each time the file runs. The same files make a second test gym named "RAM S FITNESS CLUB IMPACT" (code RAMS01). Anyone who types either code in the member app joins that gym, sees the old product name or another gym s name, and can place shop orders that no real desk will ever see.
expected: Test gyms live only on a test server, or are named plainly as MettleUp test gyms and cannot be joined by members.
fix_line: Rename the test gyms to the MettleUp name and keep them out of the member join, or move them to a test server
